//: A detached conversation is built as `conversation-<id>` (see `open_conversation_window` in lib.rs). Listing only `main` here granted it no window permissions at all, so its traffic lights did nothing and its title bar could not drag the window -- the frontend called `startDragging`, `minimize` and `close`, and Tauri rejected every one because the capability did not cover that label. Decorations are off on both kinds of window, so the app *is* the title bar; without these the second window had no way to be moved, resized or closed.
//autostart: Three operations, not `autostart:default`, for the same reason the store grant is enumerated: the settings toggle needs to read the current state and set it either way, and nothing else. Enabling writes a real entry under Windows' `Run` key, so disabling has to be reachable from the same place -- a preference that records `false` while the entry survives is the version of this feature that lies to the user.
//window-visibility: `hide`, `show` and `unminimize` are the close-to-tray path. The native side hides the window on close and the tray brings it back, but the frontend needs the same three to offer `Hide to tray` and to raise a window from within the app.
//http: Removed with the service seam (task 19). Harness requests leave through the `service_fetch` command, which is our own Rust and needs no capability grant -- the webview no longer names URLs, so there was nothing left for `http:default` to scope. A granted capability nothing needs is the FE-02 problem again. The `connect-src` entries for loopback came out of the CSP for the same reason.
//store: FE-02. This was `store:default`, which the generated ACL manifest expands to all fourteen store operations (load, get-store, set, get, has, delete, clear, reset, keys, values, entries, length, reload, save) on any file the webview names. The appearance feature calls exactly five of them against exactly one file: `load` opens `preferences.json`, then `get`, `set`, `delete`, `save` (src/design/theme/appearance.ts:58, 76, 83/97, 119, 84/98/120). Those five are what is granted now. A path scope was wanted here too and is not available: tauri-plugin-store 2.4.4 declares `global_scope_schema: null` in gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json, so the plugin defines no scope vocabulary and there is nothing to pin `preferences.json` with. The file therefore remains reachable by name only, and the standing rule stands on its own: this store is plaintext JSON in the app config dir and no credential ever enters it.
